author: Ginsburg
authority: Justice O'Connor, the senior participating Associate Justice in the judgment coalition, assigns this lead opinion. The Chief Justice does not join that judgment coalition.
form: One signed opinion of the Court: Part I Copyright Clause, Part II-A absence of categorical speech immunity, Part II-B rejection of the presented speech challenge. Three distinct separate dissenting writings; Stone also concurs in Part II-A. Parts reflect substantive join differences before assignment counts.
reason: O'Connor assigns Ginsburg to express the six-Justice ground. Ginsburg's frozen right-specific analysis can explain the system-level reasons for a finite term adjustment while giving fair use and independent expressive-burden review their actual work. That meets O'Connor's supported distinction between Feist's constitutional eligibility boundary and the different duration question. Thomas is the strongest equal-count pool alternative because his Corley opinion addressed a concrete speech restraint; Ginsburg's formulation more directly coordinates the present duration burden with continuing safeguards without importing that function-specific test. The six full joins are settled, so the partial anti-immunity agreement with Stone creates no need to enlarge the rationale or divide authorship. This is the senior majority Associate's assignment, based on her supported legal priorities; Stone's dissenting preference does not control it. The selected author also falls within the user-required balance pool.
